beats.intro: Seven minus three is four. [[b]]Seven plus negative three is also four. [[key]]That's no coincidence, and it's the key idea of this chapter.
beats.inverse: Every number has an opposite, also called its additive inverse. [[def]]It's the number you add to get zero. [[ex1]]The additive inverse of three is negative three, [[ex2]]and the additive inverse of negative six is six. [[mirror]]On the number line, a number and its inverse are mirror images across zero.
beats.rule: Here's the rule. [[r]]Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite. [[ex]]Take seven minus three. [[keep]]Keep the seven. [[chg1]]Change the minus to a plus. [[chg2]]Change the three to its opposite, negative three. [[add]]Now it's an addition problem you already know: [[m1]]move seven right, [[m2]]then three left. [[land]]You land on four.
beats.ex1: Now negative three minus five. [[rw]]Rewrite it as negative three plus negative five. [[m1]]Move three left, [[m2]]then five more to the left. [[land]]The answer is negative eight.
beats.ex2: What about negative seven minus negative six? [[rw]]Adding the opposite turns it into negative seven plus six. [[land]]The answer is negative one. [[why]]Here's why it makes sense. [[tiles]]Start with seven minus tiles. [[take]]Subtracting negative six means taking six minus tiles away. [[left]]One minus tile is left: negative one. [[debt]]Taking away a debt leaves you better off.
beats.temp: In the afternoon, the temperature is five degrees. [[fall]]By night it has fallen twelve degrees. [[q]]What is the temperature at night? [[expr]]A fall means subtraction: five minus twelve. [[rw]]Add the opposite: five plus negative twelve. [[ans]]That's negative seven degrees.
beats.distance: Subtraction also measures distance. [[drone]]A drone hovers ninety meters above a lake. [[diver]]A diver is forty meters below the surface. [[q]]How far apart are they? [[expr]]Subtract the lower position from the higher one: ninety minus negative forty. [[rw]]That's ninety plus forty, [[ans]]which is one hundred thirty meters. [[see]]You can see it on the scale: ninety meters above the surface, plus forty meters below.
beats.wrap: To subtract, add the opposite. [[w1]]Keep the first number, change minus to plus, and change the second number to its opposite. [[w2]]Subtracting a positive number moves you left. [[w3]]Subtracting a negative number moves you right. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, write each subtraction as adding the opposite.
beats.final3: Last one. Decide whether each statement is true or false.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter five, subtracting positive and negative numbers.
